key_insight: Agents-A1 shows that a 35B Mixture-of-Experts agent can reach trillion-parameter-level performance by scaling the agent horizon instead of only scaling model size. The paper argues that longer, richer agent trajectories and broader agent capabilities can deliver outsized performance gains.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of achieving frontier-level performance without continuously increasing parameter count. It tackles the limits of traditional scaling by focusing on long-horizon reasoning, action planning, and heterogeneous agent skills.
method: Build a long-horizon knowledge-action infrastructure that links external knowledge, actions, observations, and verifier feedback.
Generate and train on agentic trajectories with very long context spans, averaging about 45K tokens.
Scale agent horizons in two ways: longer trajectories and broader heterogeneous agent abilities via a MoE agent design.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more efficient path to high performance: improve how agents think, act, and learn over long horizons rather than only making models bigger. It may reduce the need for massive parameter scaling while improving real-world agentic behavior.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing knowledge -> action -> observation -> verifier feedback loops.
A comparison chart of 35B Agent vs trillion-parameter-level performance.
A timeline/trajectory graphic illustrating long-horizon agent episodes (45K tokens).
An icon set for tools, memory, planning, and verification to represent agent abilities.
paper_title: Scaling the Horizon, Not the Parameters: Reaching Trillion-Parameter Performance with a 35B Agent
paper_authors: Lei Bai, Zongsheng Cao, Yang Chen, Zhiyao Cui, Shangheng Du
